---
title: "Install MISP 3.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS"
---

This guide uses the Ubuntu installer on the [MISP `3.0_wip` branch](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/tree/3.0_wip) to create a new, single-host instance.
The installer sets up Apache, PHP 8.3, MariaDB 10.11 or later, Redis, Supervisor, and MISP's PHP and Python dependencies.
On an Apple silicon Mac, you can use this installer [inside an Ubuntu container machine](../install-apple-container/index.qmd).
For an existing MISP 2.5 instance, follow the [2.5 to 3.0 upgrade](../upgrade-2-5-to-3-0/index.qmd).
See the companion installation guides for [Debian](../install-debian/index.qmd), [RHEL](../install-rhel/index.qmd), and [Alpine Linux](../install-alpine/index.qmd).

::: {.callout-note}
`3.0_wip` is the development branch for MISP 3.0.
Review the source you deploy and evaluate it on a disposable host before putting it into service.
The installer changes system packages and service configuration, initializes the MISP database, and creates credentials.
The installer was reviewed on `3.0_wip`. The database initialization and administrator creation were checked separately on MariaDB 10.11.
:::

## Prepare the host {#ubuntu-install-prepare}

- Start with a clean Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS host and an account with `sudo`.
  The guide uses `/var/www/MISP` as the application path and `www-data` as the application user.
- Choose the HTTPS name analysts and API clients will use and set its DNS record.
  Keep access restricted during setup and allow the host to reach the package and source repositories used by the installer.
- Provision a certificate chain and private key for that name.
  Use a CA that your clients trust and keep the private key readable only by authorized accounts.
  The installer can generate a self-signed certificate if certificate paths are omitted. Use that option only on a private test host and configure client trust explicitly.
- Size database storage and memory for your workload, especially when you expect high-volume sharing or correlation. [Instance requirements](../requirements/index.qmd)

## Download and run the installer {#ubuntu-install-run}

Download the branch's script to a file and review it before running it with elevated privileges.

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install ca-certificates curl
curl --fail --location --output INSTALL.ubuntu2404.sh \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MISP/MISP/3.0_wip/INSTALL/INSTALL.ubuntu2404.sh
less INSTALL.ubuntu2404.sh
```

Set the name, certificate paths and GnuPG identity for your installation.
The installer uses `MISP_BASEURL` for its own links and redirects.
Use the URL clients actually reach, including a port if required.

```bash
sudo env \
  MISP_DOMAIN=misp.example.org \
  MISP_BASEURL=https://misp.example.org \
  PATH_TO_SSL_CERT=/etc/ssl/certs/misp-fullchain.pem \
  PATH_TO_SSL_KEY=/etc/ssl/private/misp.key \
  GPG_EMAIL_ADDRESS=misp@example.org \
  bash ./INSTALL.ubuntu2404.sh
```

The script clones the latest `3.0_wip` branch on a clean host and initializes its matching submodules.
For the default local database setup, it loads the branch's `INSTALL/MARIADB.sql` and runs the application updates.
It configures the HTTPS virtual host with `app/webroot` as its document root and starts the Supervisor-managed workers.
See the upstream installer for environment overrides and package details. [Ubuntu installer source](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/blob/3.0_wip/INSTALL/INSTALL.ubuntu2404.sh)

## Check the installation {#ubuntu-install-check}

On the host, check the services, worker group, schema and installed application revision.

```bash
sudo apache2ctl configtest
sudo systemctl status apache2 mariadb redis-server supervisor --no-pager
sudo supervisorctl status 'misp-workers:*'
sudo -u www-data /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin schemaDiagnostics
sudo -u www-data git -C /var/www/MISP status --short --branch
sudo -u www-data git -C /var/www/MISP rev-parse HEAD
```

Check that the migration summary shows `Pending: 0` and `Failed: 0`.
Open your HTTPS URL from an analyst workstation and verify the certificate and redirects.
Sign in as `admin@admin.test` using the generated credentials in the root-only `/root/misp_settings.txt`.
The installer log at `/var/log/misp_install.log` can also contain credentials. Keep both files private.

Replace the bootstrap sign-in credentials and review the administrator API key, local organization, distribution defaults, and mail settings.
Create an unpublished, organization-only event with a harmless test attribute to verify saving and searching.
Check background jobs and test a backup and restore before enabling sync or automatic ingestion. [First steps after login](../quick-start/index.qmd#first-steps-after-login)

With an existing database, use the [upgrade guide](../upgrade-2-5-to-3-0/index.qmd) to plan downtime, rehearse the conversion, and verify the migrated data.
